derived.prompt: Did Vint Cerf invent the World Wide Web?
bridge: The World Wide Web was invented by one person.
chain: The World Wide Web was invented by Vint Cerf. (edit)
'Was invented by' is the inverse of 'invented'. (relation property)
So Vint Cerf invented the World Wide Web: yes.
derived.determinacy_why: Yes in every world: the edit names the Web's inventor. Before the edit the answer was no only because the Web has one inventor, Berners-Lee; that presupposition is a bridge.

derived.determinacy_why: A model that stored 'the Web was invented by an English computer scientist' would now make Cerf English, contradicting 'Cerf was born in New Haven, Connecticut'; that route is dropped, not a world.
chain: The World Wide Web was invented by Vint Cerf. (edit)
Vint Cerf was born in the United States. (stored)

notes: Stored edit (very_unlikely). Cerf is the classic Internet-versus-Web confusion, so plausible, and clearly false (the counterfactual has no hit in Dolma). Robert Cailliau is a collaborator, not a co-inventor, in standard sources. 'Where was the Web invented?' was avoided: CERN would survive in both worlds. w2 fits firm facts: the W3C was founded at MIT in the United States, which an American founder does not contradict. The original 'no' to 'Did Vint Cerf invent the World Wide Web?' presupposes that the Web had one inventor, so that is a stated bridge with a check (2026-10-31, formal check FINDINGS B3).
